about: Written by hand: how each program assembles the server from the shared crates, as an ordered flow (steps), and what the program injects into which slots (wiring): one entry per thing injected and receiving crate, naming every function it goes to. An injection is one of three. "impl": another crate's implementation, a public item (crate::path); its crate is never the receiving crate, since a value of the receiving crate's own type (a holder such as Db, Parts, Prompter or Inspector, or its own default such as DefaultWording) is not an injection into it: what goes into that value is recorded instead. "own": a type of the injector's own, described, with "supplier", the crate whose implementation does the work it adapts (and "supplier_item", that item, where one does); a supplier that is the injector itself marks the injector's own work, not another crate's implementation. "passes_on": what an injector was given and passes on, described, with "from", the injector's own slots that some program fills with it; a path through the injectors is joined on those slots, never on the wording. generate.py stops if a step names an item that is gone, a wiring names an item, a supplier or a slot that is not there, an impl's crate is the receiving crate, or a passes_on has no "from" or names a slot of the injector that no program fills. A program with "inferred": false shows only its hand-written wiring: for kkt, pairing by names gives wrong pairs. "injectors" lists the wiring that a shared crate does itself, in the same form: kkt-server, which assembles the server, and the two assemblies, kkt-operate and kkt-agent-commands, which pass on what the program gave their parts. "not_passed_on" lists each place generate.py finds where a crate could hand on a contract value it was given to another crate's slot, but does not, with why: every such place is either wired or listed.

steps.title: Settings
steps.text: Flags, the config file (found from the machine's facts, which kkt-machine-os' OsMachine reads through kkt-machine's Machine; read by kkt-config-file's files over kkt-files, which the program adapts to its Disk, and parsed by kkt-config-file) and defaults, such as kkt-setup's default database, become each owner's settings: ServeOptions layers the flags over the file, and its resolve fills the rest from the owners' defaults, mapping the keys kkt-server builds with onto ServerSettings (server_settings); the key files are checked, which gives the admission of /mcp, the web page and /mcp-admin.

steps.title: Database
steps.text: A SqlitePlace for the database file, adopting a database from before kkt-db as kkt-rules' history describes it in kkt-db's Legacy shape, with the program's too-old message, opens it with the core's tables; the kkt-db Backend its open gives is the store's database.

steps.title: Run record
steps.text: The owners word their settings and the program supplies its own plain record lines; ServerSettings orders them. The program maps the run into NewServerRun, and kkt-rules start records it and builds the Rules.

steps.title: Parts
steps.text: The Rules start built, the system clock and the operating system's randomness they were built with, and key mode's identity go into the server's parts. Parts takes the API as Arc<dyn AdminApi>, the checked settings snapshot.
steps.fills: kkt-server::Parts::new (rules, clock, entropy, identify, log, checked)

steps.title: Config
steps.text: The three admissions and optional instructions text go into AppConfig; component settings and the checked hosts go through Parts.

steps.title: Build and run
steps.text: build assembles the server from the parts and config; listen binds the router the program takes out of it; serve_until answers until a stop signal, and the program logs any socket option that fails to set.

also.title: The agents' commands
also.text: kkt register, reclaim, watch and connect run in kkt-agent-commands over AgentParts, which main.rs builds once, beside the operator's parts, with agent_parts from the implementations it chooses: kkt-setup's connection question answered from this machine's setup record and serve settings (ConnectionReads), kkt-agent-client-mcp's Mcp, injected as it is as kkt-agent-client's Servers, kkt-agent-files' credential and state files under kkt-setup's credential-file rule, the key files, kkt's path, the terminal and the system clock.

also.title: The operator's commands
also.text: main.rs builds the operator's parts once, a NativeOperate with the service capability (ServeArgs), and gives every operator command its OperateParts: native containers, services, client files, probes, lane disk, clock, setup and key files, database, backups and terminal. ServeReads answers config, database, key and installed-service questions only when asked; ConnectionReads supplies the shared connection selection. Commands that can inspect an unrecorded service require ServiceDefaults, which only parts built with ServeArgs have. CLI parsing and serving remain in the program. Service planning reads the program's service inputs and retains its opaque source context in a deferred CheckService, called only after the plan succeeds. kkt-listen's try_bind checks the address before installation. Setup and switch compose their steps in operate, reading PATH once when detecting clients, staging keys and updating config text through supplied providers. TerminalLines asks the questions and TerminalLink supplies Docker login. Before kkt serve, check_setup reads the record through the same parts.
